lines: Registro: cotidiano gentil; cuidadora.
Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Registro: enigmático, profético, frio.
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.
Nosuri — `voice_criticality: medium`. Fora-da-lei atrevida e malandra; "aliada da justiça" irônica; oportunista. Registro coloquial/esperto.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Ougi — `voice_criticality: low`. Irmão da Nosuri; pragmático, parceria com a irmã.
Registro: confuso, desorientado, semi-consciente.
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Rulutieh — `voice_criticality: medium`. Princesa tímida e gentil; hesitante (gagueja quando nervosa: "P-Princesa..."), educada, se anima ao falar de arte/BL. Não soar arrogante apesar de princesa.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Anomalia 0x33f9 — texto PT/EN corrompido na fonte
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar a linha `0x33f9` como anomalia de fonte (não traduzir em cima do lixo; tratar como linha de sistema reescrita). **Razão:** A string original já vem misturada PT/EN e truncada ("...SISTEMAS AM . RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. Endereço da string = `file_start_do_site + uint32`. Prova: dos ~47k sites, **42.101** só apontam para string como file-relativos vs **63**

lines.source: Bodyguards...?
Correct. I would have you act as security detail\n
for a particular group of officials.
After I answer Oshtor's summons, he greets me\n
with a strange assignment.
Tomorrow, ambassadors from a certain nation\n
will be arriving in the imperial capital.
They are from a country far to the west of\n
Yamato... An island nation beyond the seas.
Huh. Must be a real hassle, coming all the way\n
here.
They are indeed a much smaller country than\n
Yamato, but my liege seems quite interested\n
in them.
Their homeland is known as... the land where\n
god sleeps.
Where god sleeps, huh...?
Naturally, we must take utmost care to ensure\n
that nothing happens to them.
That is where you come in, Lord Haku. I would\n
have you act as their protection.
Us as bodyguards, huh...
Something troubles you?
Not really. I just don't get it.
Isn't that kind of job reserved for actual\n
soldiers?
Our usual jobs aren't in the public eye.\n
Shady stuff. That's what I thought, anyway.
You need not discredit yourself.\n
I am asking you to do this because I have\n
faith in your skills.
Believe me, I'll take all the credit I can.\n
I fully understand that people like us are\n
necessary.
But I'm not so sure how that's going to come off\n
to the ambassadors.
If Yamato sends them a bunch of ragtag misfits\n
instead of soldiers, it doesn't give the best\n
impression.
I'm just saying, it might not be in Yamato's\n
best interests to send us if it might offend\n
them.
Haha... A keen eye, as ever. You truly are\n
full of surprises.
Very well. Then allow me to speak with complete\n
honesty.
With that, Oshtor suddenly rises...
And strides into the backroom, abruptly leaving\n
me behind.
Hey! Sorry for the wait.
Ukon scratches his head as he ambles back,\n
and flumps back down onto his seat.
Whew. Feels a lot more natural to talk to you\n
when I'm back to this look.
I see. Well, honestly, I don't really care\n
which one I'm talking to.
Man, this guy's as complicated as ever...\n
Well, I guess I'm kind of used to it by now.
...Well, where was I?
Of course, we'll have our soldiers guarding them\n
as well. Your group will be more like a support\n
team.
Basically, you'll be guides for the ambassadors,\n
handle their everyday needs... That kind of\n
thing.
Yeah, all right. That sounds more like our\n
style.
But, of course... This is all just a front.\n
There's actually something else I want you\n
to do, kid.
I figured you were going somewhere with this...
So, what exactly do you need me to do?
Put plainly... I want you to observe them.
Observe?
Yep. Yamato's only had a bit of trade contact\n
with this island nation. Nothing big or\n
official.
Of course, we've got all their basic info.
The state of their country, their government,\n
their military might...\n
The usual stuff.
But it's all just words on a page. Can't jump\n
to any conclusions about them based on that\n
alone.
...Guess you have a point.
I want you to trust your own eyes, your own\n
ears, your own senses... Learn all you can\n
about them.
We need to learn whether or not this country\n
of theirs can be a good ally for Yamato...
...And that's pretty much it.
*Sigh*... I should have known my dear brother\n
would devise something like this.
So these ambassadors are arriving in the\n
imperial capital soon.
Hmmm. I wonder what kind of people they are?
But it will be a little while until we are\n
officially appointed as their bodyguards,\n
correct?
Yeah. In the meantime, let's see what these\n
foreign ambassadors look like.
Hm... I see. I was wondering why you gathered\n
us here on the main street. So that was your\n
plan...
Hm?
I look over to see Kuon holding a steaming cup.
What're you drinking there, Kuon?
Huh? Oh, it was a little chilly today, so I\n
bought some warm tea from the vendor over\n
there.
Huh. This market sells practically anything you\n
could think of, doesn't it?
So, what country exactly are these ambassadors\n
representing?
Oh, it was an island country to the west of\n
The name was something like...\n
To... Tuss...?
Oh, right. It was Tuskur.
Pffffft!!
Kuon immediately spits the tea she's drinking...\n
straight into the nearby Atuy's face.
Ack! Hot!!
S-Sorry, Atuy!!
You caught me completely off my guard there...
I'm so sorry... Let me wipe that off for you.
Um... Miss Kuon, do you know something about\n
this Tuskur country?
What kind of nation is it?
Huh? Wh-Whatever are you talking about?\n
I have no idea, I think--not the slightest!
She's an open book. She must know a lot about\n
this country...
B-But I suppose I... I may have heard it\n
mentioned before, I think!
I-I see... So Tuskur has...\n
Hmmm...
She mutters to herself as she rubs furiously\n
at Atuy's face with a cloth.
*Rub* *rub* *rub* *rub*
Owie... Kuon!? That huuurts!
You heard of them before, Nekone?
I have not heard much about them.\n
All I know is that they are a small island\n
nation to the west.
That must have been quite the journey for them.\n
To have crossed the sea to come all the way\n
here...
Yeah, right? And I hear one of the officials\n
coming here is a kamunagi or something.\n
Someone important.
A kamunagi...!?
*Grind* *grind* *grind* *grind*
Kuon's grip tightens on the cloth in her hand.
Owowowowowow! Kuon, you're hurting me!\n
You're going to grate my skin off at this\n
rate!
Oh! S-S-S-Sorry! I wasn't paying attention!!
This visiting kamunagi... It must be difficult\n
for her, being in a completely different land.
Indeed. I would like to be of service to her,\n
regardless of her station.
Agreed.
I'm sure that concern would only go to waste.\n
They're not the type to be daunted by such\n
things.
Huh? How would you know that?
W-Well, that's...
I-In any case! I think we should reject this\n
job.
Huh!?
I don't think we need to be the ones to handle\n
such an assignment.
If these people are strange enough to cross\n
an entire ocean to come here, we should let\n
them be.
I mean, they might not even like the fact that\n
they're getting bodyguards, you know?
...You're acting rather cold today, Kuon.
You are not acting like your usual self,\n
dear sister.
E-Er...
Eeep!?
Aha. It would seem the dignitaries in question\n
have arrived.
We look back to see a number of carriages\n
heading our way from off in the distance.
We can hear the cheering of the crowd as the\n
carriages pass.
Wha--!? What are those steeds?\n
There's not a single hair on them!
You are right...
The woptors pulling the carriages look pretty\n
strange.
They make an odd sight compared to the woptors\n
from Yamato. Instead of a light fur, their skin\n
is scaly.
Well, Tuskur's climate is much warmer...
Oh... So that's what it is.
Wait, how do you even know that, Kuon?
O-Oh, you know... I just remember reading it\n
somewhere.
I must say, this is quite the spectacle...
It's... so beautiful...
The carriages pulled by these furless woptors\n
also have very strange decorations over them.
It's not flashy, but it has a delicate yet\n
elaborate pattern... just enough not to be\n
gaudy.
Even someone without an eye for this stuff\n
can tell their culture has a different style\n
from Yamato's.
Oh, look!
The window on the carriage slides open to reveal\n
a woman inside.
Immediately, we hear gasps from the crowd.
She's... extremely beautiful.
Her glossy pale cyan hair is neatly cut to\n
around her shoulders, and her face has a\n
gentle smile.
What draws the most of our attention, however,\n
are the large black wings on her back.
I've seen all kinds since we came to the\n
imperial capital, but never anyone with wings.
Could that person be the kamunagi?
I'd say that's a safe bet.
Uruuru and Saraana suddenly glide in front of\n
me, glaring at her as if to scare her away.
Worrying that she might be offended, I send\n
them back, and take a good look at the foreign\n
kamunagi.
She looks very gentle, and so elegant...\n
Pretty much the complete opposite of Kuon...
...Huh?
...I suddenly realize that I've lost track of\n
Kuon.
I glance around, and see her trying to sidle\n
inconspicuously into an alleyway.
What do you think you're doing?
I-I'm not doing anything.
Quit skulking around. Why don't you take a good\n
look at the people we're supposed to be\n
guarding?
I-I'm not hiding! And besides, they really have\n
no need for bodyguards anyway.
Yeah, like that excuse is gonna fly. C'mon...
I struggle to pull Kuon out of the alleyway\n
as she tries desperately to hide herself...\n
for some reason.
As the kamunagi looks around her new\n
surroundings eagerly, we happen to lock eyes.
...*Grin*
Huh?
*Wave*
I'm not sure why, but the kamunagi suddenly\n
smiles and begins to wave.
Huh? What? Is she waving at me?
I don't really get it, but I figure I might\n
as well wave back.
The kamunagi smiles back at me, apparently\n
satisfied.
The carriage eventually passes us, and disappears\n
into the crowd of people.
Wooooow... She was sooo pretty.
Yes... I don't think I've ever seen someone\n
so beautiful before...
Atuy and Rulutieh are still giddy with\n
excitement after seeing the woman.
Was she... waving at me?
But if she was, then... why?
As I bemusedly watch the procession move on,\n
another shocking sight fills my view.
Rrwr?
Bwah!?
A giant white beast trudges forth.\n
It's huge--easily bigger than a normal person.
Wh-What the hell!?
The previously boisterous crowd suddenly goes\n
quiet.
The beast seems completely unbothered as it\n
continues along the main street.
The crowd holds its breath as they watch it,\n
but they don't seem afraid. More like...\n
in awe?
Wh-What in the world is THAT beast!?
Please stay your hand, dear sister.
Nosuri reaches for her bow instinctively,\n
but Ougi calmly stops her.
Look.
Ougi points his finger in its direction.
Around the giant four-legged beast appear to be\n
its guards, following along as they keep a\n
lookout.
The fact that they're more wary of their\n
surroundings than the beast itself shows how\n
much they trust it.
That means... that thing is from Tuskur as\n
well...?
They even sent Mukkuru...?
You say something, Kuon?
Huh!? Uh, no. I didn't say anything!
As I peer at Kuon, I realize that everything\n
is suddenly a little darker. I look back to\n
find--
...Wh--Holy--
The beast is right next to us, looming menacingly\n
over me.
It's stopped right in front of us.
Wh-Why is it looking at us?
N-N-N-Nekone! Please, get behind me!
I wouldn't make a nice meal, you know?\n
I recommend something with a little more fat.
Wh--!? Hey, s-stop pushing me!\n
And I am definitely NOT fat!
Suddenly, the back of the beast seems to\n
bulge up.
Over the frizzy fur, a girl pokes her face out.
Even my fear disappears from the surprise.
She's just as beautiful as the woman with the\n
wings.
But she feels a little more... approachable.\n
A different kind of charm--more mysterious.
Perched on her shoulder is a small furry white\n
creature.
*Stare*
Wait, why is she staring at me?
H-Hi there.
I give in and give her a friendly smile, but\n
the beast and the girl continue to stare at me.
This is a little weird...
I suddenly realize I'm still holding onto\n
Kuon's hand.
I look around to see Kuon shrinking back,\n
a guilty expression on her face for some\n
reason.
...What the hell is going on?
...*Smile*
Did she just... smile at me?
Just as I think that, the giant beast suddenly\n
turns its huge head around.
Before I can even figure out the reason behind\n
her smile, the massive feline is already\n
prowling away, moving down the street.
And eventually its enormous figure disappears\n
from our line of sight.
The bubble of silence pops, and the crowd\n
immediately begins murmuring again.
Crowd
What was that!? What WAS that!?\n
That thing was huge!!
Do those things just wander around freely in\n
the lands across the sea!?
The crowd's gone from being mesmerized by the\n
winged woman's beauty to this sudden uproar.
